business_scope.primary_industry_name: General Partner Management Entity for Early-Stage Technology Funds

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Unitary National; continental European notarial system followed by Commercial Registry registration)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement between the Kingdom of Spain and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (1990, in force 1992)
EU–Latin America and Caribbean modernized Association Agreements (in particular the EU–Chile Advanced Framework Agreement, signed 2023, pending ratification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 3, 4, 6, 14, 31 y 37), as amended by Ley 11/2018, de 28 de diciembre; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 (arts. 3-10 y 39-40); Orden JUS/319/2018, de 6 de marzo, por la que se crea el Registro de Titularidades Reales de la Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado; Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del Procedimiento Administrativo Común de las Administraciones Públicas.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social (negative name clearance certificate issued by the Central Commercial Registry; original presented to the Spanish notary when executing the incorporation deed)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic_Notarization_Only (no apostille required for domestic use; a Hague Apostille can be affixed if the certificate is later presented to a foreign authority)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Escritura de Constitución (notarized incorporation deed of the SL) together with the Estatutos Sociales (bylaws) executed before a licensed Spanish notary; statutory notarization requirement under Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, art. 20
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the Notarial College of the chosen registered office jurisdiction (e.g., Colegio Notarial de Madrid)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic_Notarization_Only (complete notarial protocol registered at the Registro Mercantil Provincial)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Vigencia) of the corporate founding shareholder and, where relevant, of the Spanish or foreign venture capital fund to be managed by the GP
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registry or Companies House of the founding shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague_Apostille (for countries party to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961); otherwise Consular_Legalization before the Spanish Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies, proof of residential address, and curriculum vitae of all proposed directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), together with a signed UBO disclosure statement under art. 4 Ley 10/2010 identifying the natural-person ultimate owners holding directly or indirectly 25% or more of the capital or voting rights or exercising control by other means
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the country of origin or a Spanish notary completing statutory identification statements (diligencia de identificación)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague_Apostille_or_Consular_Legalization (depending on the origin country), followed by certified Spanish translation by a sworn translator (traductor jurado)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement covering the future capital calls and the initial share capital subscription of the founding shareholder (minimum SL share capital of EUR 3,000)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank of the founding shareholder in the country of origin (regulated financial institution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague_Apostille (if issued in a Hague Convention member state); Consular_Legalization for non-member states; accompanied by sworn Spanish translation where required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse-media and sanctions screening of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list (1267/1988 resolutions), (iii) the OFAC SDN list (required because the target payment rails include USD SWIFT transfers), (iv) the SEPBLAC – Banco de España injunctions and administrative sanctions register, and (v) the CNMV disciplinary register. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified in accordance with art. 14 Ley 10/2010 and art. 15 Real Decreto 304/2014; any PEP nexus triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence (EDD) including source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and intensified transaction monitoring. Screening results must be evidenced in the pre-incorporation AML file and re-run immediately prior to execution of the deed and before any capital call.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online platform: www.rmc.es (name clearance via the 'Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social' application); standard online incorporation may also be initiated through the CIRCE system (www.circe.es) for plain SL formations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Pursuant to art. 402 of the Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (RRM), the company name must be composed of Spanish-language terms or universally used Latin-script expressions; the name must be written in Spanish orthography, and non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters following the rules of the Cervantes Institute. The abbreviation 'S.L.' or the full denomination 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' is mandatory. Identical, phonetically identical, or notoriously similar existing names are rejected by the Registro Mercantil Central per art. 408 RRM.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Capital Riesgo / Entidad de Capital Riesgo – requires prior CNMV authorization under Ley 22/2014, de 12 de noviembre; not permitted at name-clearance stage unless the license application is pending
Banco, Caja, Financiera, Finanzas – banking terms requiring prior authorization of the Banco de España (art. 406.2 RRM)
Seguros, Reaseguros – insurance terms requiring prior authorization of the Dirección General de Seguros y Fondos de Pensiones
España, Nacional, Gobierno, Administración, Ministerio – terms reserved for public entities or requiring ministerial authorization (art. 404 RRM)
Sociedad Anónima, S.A., S.A.U., S.Com. por A., Colectiva, Comanditaria – corporate-type words inconsistent with the SL form
Oficial, Colegio, Cámara, Certificado – terms suggesting regulated professional bodies or public credentialing
Internacional – accepted only where the corporate purpose objectively demonstrates cross-border activity; otherwise rejected as misleading
Holding, Grupo – permitted only with documented controlling activity over subsidiaries
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The certification is valid for three months from issue and is not extendable; if the incorporation deed is not executed within that window the name reverts to the public pool and a new application must be filed. Upon administrative rejection of a proposed denomination, the applicant may (a) re-file a new application with up to five alternate names in order of preference at the Registro Mercantil Central; (b) submit a written response to the RMC registrar's initial objection, including evidence of distinctiveness or prior legitimate use; or (c) file an appeal ('recurso de alzada') before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Cortes within one month following notification, pursuant to arts. 325-326 RRM and arts. 112 and 121 Ley 39/2015. The DGSJFP must resolve the appeal within three months; failure to resolve constitutes administrative silence, which is deemed negative for the applicant, allowing subsequent judicial review before the Audiencia Nacional. In the interim, urgent incorporations may proceed with a re-filed name request, but the notary will not authorize the deed without an effective negative name certificate.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is permissible solely for the initial commercial registry registration provided it corresponds to a physical postal address in Spain where official notifications may lawfully be served (arts. 9 and 10 Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010). However, for this specific venture capital general partner entity, a pure virtual mailbox without physical management premises, personnel, and documentary substance fails the CNMV's fit-and-proper and effective-board test and will lead to refusal or revocation of the SGEIC/GP license; SEPBLAC likewise requires the implementation of AML procedures and records at a physical establishment. The registered office must be adapted to a genuine operational office in Madrid, Barcelona, or Valencia before the CNMV license application is submitted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: A quantified 70% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months after the entity becomes operational and licensed by CNMV/SEPBLAC, reflecting the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML tier applicable to a venture capital GP using SWIFT/capital-call wires; SEPBLAC's routine inspection cycle for regulated obliged entities and CNMV's continuous supervisory protocol for managers of alternative closed-ended investment vehicles (art. 33 Ley 35/2003, de 4 de noviembre, de Instituciones de Inversión Colectiva, as amended; Ley 22/2014) mandate regular unannounced site visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name clearance certificate – Certificación Negativa de Denominación (two name proposals in a single application)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry, Madrid)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official tariff for the RMC name request (approx. EUR 36 plus VAT; incremental fee per additional name proposal)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial execution of the incorporation deed (Escritura de Constitución) and notarization of the Estatutos Sociales (bylaws)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary of the Notarial College of the registered office jurisdiction (regulated tariff – Real Decreto 1426/1989, Arancel Notarial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial arancel computed on share capital (standard SL capital EUR 3,000–5,000), plus protocol book, copy, and notary-assistant statutory fees; market benchmark EUR 600–900 for a standard SL deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mercantile Registry registration fee – inscripción de la sociedad in the Registro Mercantil Provincial
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registrar's statutory arancel under Real Decreto 1427/1989, computed on share capital and number of registration entries; benchmark EUR 450–600 for an SL with EUR 3,000–5,000 capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal consultation, CNMV licensing feasibility memo on the general partner management model, and corporate governance drafting (managers' powers, capital-call procedures, conflicts policy)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Spanish business law firm (notary or registry authority receives no part of this fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market hourly benchmark EUR 250–400 per hour; fixed package estimate for the Stage 1 scope including tax and regulatory memo

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, KYC/AML pre-incorporation file, PEP and sanctions screening of all directors and ultimate beneficial owners (EU/UN/OFAC/SEPBLAC/CNMV lists)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML compliance consultant / lawyer (future Data Protection Officer and AML Compliance Officer candidate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed scope package for a medium-risk regulated GP; includes background checks per natural person and consolidating the mandatory file under art. 31 Ley 10/2010

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn Spanish translation (traducción jurada) of all apostilled foreign corporate documents, passports, bank references, and UBO statements
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Official sworn translators appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs, European Union and Cooperation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-page tariff of the sworn translators (approx. EUR 80–120 per page, depending on complexity and urgency); bundle estimate for 4–6 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign corporate documents and notarized ID copies at the competent authority of the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / designated apostille authority of the origin country; Spanish Consulate for consular legalization where the Hague Convention does not apply
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official government legalization tariff (approx. EUR 35–70 per document) plus courier and certified translation coordination

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service – physical location with postal handling in Madrid (adapted for later CNMV licensing and SEPBLAC inspections)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual rate for a virtual-plus-physical office package in Madrid (EUR 700–1,100/year); upgraded to full serviced office upon license application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) application and appointment for one foreign director / general partner representative (additional NIE per extra director)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Consulate in the director's country of residence / Spanish National Police (Oficina de Extranjería)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory consular fee (Tasa EX-15 / Tasa T-12, approx. EUR 8–12) plus administrative handling and apostilled supporting documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening for the deposit of share capital and future investor capital calls (SWIFT/SEPA rails)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial bank in Spain (corporate account contract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank account administration and file-opening fee, prevailing market benchmark EUR 0–200; no statutory public fee; includes bank's own KYC/AML screening of UBOs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 4 bis, 19-23, 30-35, 159-197, 210-241 and 272-279. If the entity manages venture capital or other closed-ended investment vehicles, Law 22/2014, including its authorization, capital, governance, conduct and reporting provisions for sociedades gestoras de entidades de inversión colectiva de tipo cerrado, also applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The relevant Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, coordinated through the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), including the articles of association, filed electronically with the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry. The company acquires legal personality upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. No statutory escrow account is required, although a bank certificate evidencing cash contribution is commonly obtained. If capital is below EUR 3,000, statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules apply until the prescribed threshold is reached. Any additional capital or own-funds requirement applicable to an SGEIC or regulated investment manager is separate and may be materially higher.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the shares subscribed by the incorporators are confirmed as fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted; (3) [name] is appointed Sole Director, or the persons listed in Schedule 1 are appointed directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; (4) [name] is appointed attorney for tax, registry, banking and licensing filings; and (5) management shall obtain the company tax identification number, open the corporate bank account, maintain statutory books and implement applicable AML, regulatory and accounting controls.
incorporation_legal_framework.fee_qualification: The EUR 0 amount represents no fixed state incorporation charge and the exemption from transfer tax and stamp duty applicable to incorporation. Notarial, Commercial Registry, publication, legalization, translation and municipal charges are separate variable costs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-certification service or authorized filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names in priority order and request a negative name certificate. The certificate must be issued in the intended company's name and remain valid for the statutory reservation period. Use the exact certified name in the deed, articles and tax filings.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace unavailable or confusingly similar names and resubmit. If the certificate contains an error, request correction before executing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain foreign-investor identification and tax credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) and the competent police or consular channel for foreigner identification numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an NIE for each non-resident individual director, shareholder or authorized representative requiring Spanish tax identification. Obtain an NIF for non-resident corporate shareholders and evidence of existence, incumbency and authority. Apostille or legalize foreign documents and provide sworn Spanish translations where required.
required_dossiers: NIE applications and powers of attorney
Foreign corporate certificates of incorporation and good standing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure documentary defects, replace expired certificates, submit missing apostilles or translations, and refile through the competent AEAT or consular channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (notario) selected for the registered office jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare articles covering corporate purpose, registered office, share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance, financial year and profit allocation. Evidence full payment of cash contributions through a bank certificate or the statutory alternative declaration in the deed. Execute the public deed personally or through a duly legalized and translated power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Bank certificate or statutory contribution declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct notarial observations, replace defective powers, provide missing ownership evidence, and execute a rectifying deed if the notary identifies an execution or drafting defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the deed with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) of the registered office, normally through the executing notary's electronic filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the signed electronic deed, articles and supporting documents for registration. Confirm that the corporate purpose accurately distinguishes ordinary advisory activities from regulated management of collective investment undertakings. Pay applicable Registry and publication charges, which are separate from state incorporation tax.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of registry charges
Regulatory authorization evidence, if required before commencing the stated activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the registrar's qualification notice within the prescribed period, submit corrective documents or a rectifying deed, and appeal or seek judicial review under the Commercial Registry rules if the objection is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain definitive tax registration and activate statutory books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT), Commercial Registry and authorized electronic filing platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain or confirm the definitive NIF using the registered deed and Registry certificate. File the census declaration, select the applicable economic activities and tax obligations, and identify beneficial owners. Legalize the mandatory accounting and corporate books electronically through the Commercial Registry within the applicable deadlines.
required_dossiers: Electronic certificate or authorized filing mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct Form 036 inconsistencies, provide Registry evidence or beneficial-owner information, and resubmit through the AEAT electronic portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for regulated venture-capital management authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Securities Market Commission (Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores, CNMV)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before providing regulated management, submit the authorization application required for a sociedad gestora de entidades de inversión colectiva de tipo cerrado (SGEIC), or the applicable investment-firm authorization if the proposed services fall under another regulated category. File the business plan, governance framework, qualifying holdings, directors' fitness evidence, own-funds evidence, risk and compliance systems, AML controls, outsourcing arrangements and client-asset safeguards.
required_dossiers: Business plan and three-year financial projections
Compliance, risk, internal-audit and AML manuals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer CNMV information requests within the specified deadline, amend the application, replace unsuitable directors or controllers, supplement own-funds evidence, and use the applicable administrative appeal or judicial review route against a refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete municipal premises, workplace and operational clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality (Ayuntamiento) of the premises, autonomous-community occupational safety authority and, where applicable, the regional industrial authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the premises require a responsible declaration, prior communication, opening/activity licence or works permit. Obtain fire-safety and occupancy documentation, verify electrical and building installations, complete occupational risk assessments and register employers and employees with Social Security before commencing employment.
required_dossiers: Responsible declaration or municipal licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure municipal or technical observations, submit amended plans, obtain a corrected certificate, and use the applicable administrative review or appeal procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Securities Market Commission (CNMV) for regulated venture-capital management authorization; the competent autonomous-community industrial authority and municipality for premises, installations and activity controls. A pure office-based investment manager normally has no manufacturing licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorization as a Sociedad Gestora de Entidades de Inversión Colectiva de Tipo Cerrado (SGEIC), under Law 22/2014, where the entity manages venture-capital entities or other qualifying closed-ended investment vehicles. A separate municipal opening/activity licence or responsible declaration may be required for the premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from formal EIA for an ordinary office-based venture-capital management business with no industrial installation, emissions or process wastewater. Project-specific screening is required if construction, major refurbishment, generators, fuel storage or other listed activities are introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No routine process wastewater or industrial VOC discharge is expected from ordinary offices. Any discharge to public sewer must comply with the municipal or regional discharge authorization and applicable limits. Air emissions, generators and VOC-producing activities must comply with Law 34/2007, Royal Decree 100/2011 and, where applicable, Royal Decree 117/2003. Waste must be segregated, stored and transferred through authorized operators under Law 7/2022 and Royal Decree 553/2020. Hazardous waste requires documented producer and transfer controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the applicable municipal opening/activity clearance or responsible declaration, fire-protection design and certificate under Royal Decree 513/2017, and building and occupancy compliance under the Technical Building Code. Electrical, emergency lighting, HVAC and other regulated installations require authorized installer certificates and periodic inspection where applicable. Conduct workplace risk assessment, emergency planning, worker information and training under Law 31/1995 and its implementing regulations. Structural-load inspection is required where works, equipment or occupancy changes affect the building; it is not ordinarily a separate licensing condition for a standard office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Provincial/regional AEAT offices handle NIF certification, census filings, and VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign founders and administrators must first obtain an NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero). Prior to notarising the incorporation deed, request a provisional corporate NIF (CIF) from AEAT by filing Form 036; include the provisional CIF in the incorporation deed. Following registration of the deed in the Registro Mercantil (within 2 months), file the definitive declaración censal (Form 036) to confirm the definitive NIF (initial letter 'B' for an SL), disclose commencement of activity, the applicable IAE economic-activity epigraph for financial/venture-capital management services, and register for VAT (alta en IVA). Appoint a tax representative where required; obtain a Spanish digital certificate (FNMT/Cl@ve) for mandatory electronic filing of all tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — The SL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income at 25%; newly created entities may apply a reduced 15% rate for the first two fiscal years of economic activity under art. 29.3 LIS. No pass-through or transparent treatment is available under general Spanish tax law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not administer a check-the-box or elective pass-through classification; legal form determines taxation. Statutory elections relevant to a venture-capital GP entity include: (i) the 15% new-entity CIT rate (art. 29.3 LIS); (ii) fiscal consolidation group election under art. 61 LIS where the GP is owned ≥75% by a resident entity; (iii) application of the 95% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains under art. 21 LIS, subject to the 5% minimum shareholding and one-year holding period; (iv) capitalisation and levelling reserves under arts. 25–26 LIS; (v) VAT elections, including the monthly refund scheme (REDEME), SII opt-in, and intra-community operator registration; (vi) no optional hybrid-mismatch election — ATAD anti-hybrid rules under art. 15 bis LGT apply mandatorily.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Ley 37/1992), harmonised with Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No annual turnover registration threshold applies to established Spanish entities — Spanish VAT registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable economic activity. Non-EU suppliers without a Spanish establishment must register from the first transaction and appoint a VAT representative; EU suppliers of distance sales and electronically supplied services apply the pan-EU €10,000 annual threshold under art. 70.ter.3 LIVA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) under Reglamento 596/2016 imposes real-time VAT book-record reporting to AEAT via XML web services (within 8 days, or 4 days for monthly filers) for taxpayers with invoiced turnover exceeding €6,000,000 per annum and myself VAT-group members. Separately, Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) and Royal Decree 1007/2023 (VeriFactu) mandate B2B electronic invoicing for all companies, requiring an integrity-protected XML/QR hash stamp; transmission to AEAT or to an accredited private invoicing platform must occur in real time or within 4 calendar days, effectively creating a digital fiscal clearance and stamping procedure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: art. 21.1 LIVA zero-rates exports where goods physically leave EU territory, typically within 90 days of dispatch, and the exporter substantiates departure through a Customs Export Declaration (DUA) issued in its own name plus transport documentation; intra-EU supplies are exempt (not zero-rated) under art. 25 LIVA with the customer's EU VAT ID declared in VIES. Services: venture-capital management and advisory services provided to non-EU funds or non-EU investors fall outside the scope of Spanish VAT under art. 69.1.1º LIVA (B2B place-of-supply rule) where the recipient is established outside Spain and has no Spanish permanent establishment; however, management services invoiced to Spanish-resident fund investors or funds attract standard IVA at 21%, and the art. 20.1.18º LIVA exemption does not extend to the management of venture-capital/ECR funds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA — Documento Único Administrativo) validated by Spanish customs, with exporter identification, HS code, value, and exit-office stamp.

Transport document — Bill of Lading, CMR/CIM, or House/Master Air Waybill — evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU territory to the non-EU destination, consistent with DUA and commercial invoice data.

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or equivalent bank/SWIFT credit confirmation showing the export consideration credited to the SL's resident account in the invoiced currency.
Commercial invoice, packing list, EUR.1/ATR certificate (where preferential origin is claimed), and any applicable export licence or controlled-technology declaration.

For offshore services: executed management/investment-advisory agreement identifying the non-EU recipient, the recipient's foreign VAT/TIN reference, wiring/payment instructions, and documentary evidence that the recipient lacks a Spanish permanent establishment.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT cross-matches customs exit data, bank SWIFT receipts, SII records, and VIES statements to identify improper zero-rating. Upon detection, AEAT recharacterises the supply and assesses VAT at 21% on the original consideration, plus statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora). Voluntary late correction attracts escalating 1%-per-month surcharges up to 20% (art. 27 LGT); audited assessments and concealment trigger sanctions of 50%–150% of the under-declared tax (art. 191 LGT), with aggravated penalties for false invoices under art. 201 LGT, clawback of refunded input VAT, exclusion from REDEME/SII privileges, and criminal liability under art. 305 Código Penal (imprisonment of 1–5 years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount) where the annual defrauded quota exceeds €120,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank monetary and foreign-exchange framework. Spain's foreign-exchange reporting and investment-control framework is supplemented by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and the State Tax Administration Agency where applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro and has no general exchange controls between euro-area jurisdictions. Current-account payments, including management fees, dividends, interest, trade payments and ordinary service payments, are generally freely transferable, subject to anti-money-laundering, sanctions, tax and financial-sector rules. Capital-account transactions, including shareholder funding, intercompany loans, acquisitions, fund commitments and distributions, are generally permitted but may trigger statistical, foreign-investment, tax, beneficial-ownership or sectoral reporting. Profit remittance normally requires distributable accounting profits, approval of annual accounts and distributions, maintenance of mandatory legal reserves, satisfaction of creditor-protection rules, applicable withholding-tax analysis and evidence of the underlying transaction. A venture-capital general partner or manager may require authorization or registration with the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores under Law 22/2014 and applicable AIFMD rules; banking access does not replace that regulatory requirement. Transfers involving sanctioned parties, high-risk jurisdictions, opaque ownership, unexplained third-party funding or unlicensed fund-raising may be blocked or escalated by the bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank, no general mandatory conversion ratio and no universal statutory conversion deadline for ordinary export receipts. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or another permitted currency and may be held with an authorized bank, subject to contractual banking terms and accounting, tax and statistical reporting. Payment-service providers and financial institutions perform transaction and balance-of-payments reporting under applicable Spanish and European rules; direct external financial transactions may require resident reporting where a prescribed form, threshold or category applies. For this entity, the expected revenue is primarily management fees, carried interest and investment-related services rather than merchandise exports; each receipt should be classified using the bank's purpose code and supported by the management agreement, invoice, fund documentation and tax records.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for ancillary payment and collection services, low-to-medium as the sole treasury bank. A European Economic Area electronic-money institution or payment institution may provide euro payment accounts and SEPA services under passporting or local authorization, but it is not a bank, may not provide a full deposit-taking relationship, and may impose limits on investment-fund, escrow, client-money and high-value cross-border activity. Offshore or non-EEA digital EMIs require separate authorization analysis, may lack SEPA access, and commonly face correspondent-bank, sanctions, safeguarding, data, tax-reporting and source-of-funds restrictions. Client or fund assets must not be commingled with the SL's own operating funds. Use an authorized Spanish or EEA bank for regulated-fund cash, capital calls, distributions, escrow and material liquidity reserves.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors appear physically to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be available where the bank can verify the company, directors, beneficial owners and authorized signatories through legally acceptable electronic identification and documentary controls. Banks may nevertheless require an in-person meeting, qualified electronic signature, notarized or apostilled documents, Spanish tax identification numbers, video identification or branch attendance, particularly where directors or beneficial owners are non-resident, ownership is layered, the business is regulated, the expected flows are high-value or the structure involves investment funds. The bank's risk-based policy controls the practical outcome.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear distinction between the SL as a venture-capital general partner or management entity and the investment funds, investors or portfolio companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate chart; constitutional documents; registry certificate; detailed business memorandum; management and advisory agreements; fund limited partnership or equivalent constitutional documents; CNMV authorization or registration evidence where applicable; written funds-flow map; confirmation that investor and fund assets are held separately.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership cannot be established through an ownership chain, trust, nominee arrangement or foreign investment vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current ownership chart to natural persons; passports and proof of address; ultimate-beneficial-owner declaration; foreign registry extracts; trust or partnership documents; notarized powers of attorney; tax-residence certificates; explanation of control rights and voting rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transactions involve high-value capital calls, investor subscriptions, distributions or transfers to multiple jurisdictions inconsistent with the stated operating profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast; transaction-purpose matrix; fund financial model; capital-call notices; subscription agreements; distribution notices; invoices; board approvals; counterparty list; expected countries and currencies; bank statements demonstrating historical activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming funds originate from third parties, offshore vehicles, crypto-related businesses, politically exposed persons or high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds files; audited financial statements; investor onboarding records; beneficial-owner verification; sanctions and PEP screening results; subscription agreements; tax records; independent legal or compliance opinion where appropriate; documented enhanced due diligence and transaction rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The entity performs regulated investment-management, marketing, placement, custody or payment activity without clear authorization status.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulatory perimeter memorandum; CNMV authorization, registration or exemption analysis; AIFMD status; service-provider agreements; organizational chart; compliance manual; complaints and conflicts policies; confirmation that custody, depositary and payment functions are outsourced to authorized providers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors, shareholders or signatories lack Spanish tax identification or documentation is not properly legalized.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Spanish NIF/NIE documentation; legalized or apostilled corporate extracts; sworn Spanish translations where required; notarized signature authorities; proof of residential address; tax-residence certificates; board resolution appointing signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Purpose codes, invoice descriptions or accounting treatment do not match the payment pattern, including unexplained transfers between the GP, funds and portfolio companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment-purpose coding guide; reconciled general ledger; invoice register; intercompany agreements; fund accounting records; transfer-pricing support; board approvals; monthly bank reconciliations; documented approval matrix and exception log.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash, unregulated payment intermediaries or commingled client and corporate funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy prohibiting personal and cash settlement; segregated-account architecture; authorized-signatory matrix; payment workflow; bank mandate; reconciliations; remediation plan for any historical commingling; independent accountant confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-control, correspondent-banking or adverse-media concerns involving counterparties or jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening records for the entity, beneficial owners, directors and counterparties; sanctions-risk assessment; country-risk policy; transaction licenses or legal opinions where relevant; adverse-media analysis; escalation and approval records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route shareholder equity, share-premium funding and shareholder loans from the verified shareholder or lender's account directly to the SL's designated Spanish bank account. Use a clear payment narrative identifying the legal entity, instrument, agreement date and purpose, such as paid-in capital, shareholder loan or fund-management working capital. Provide the bank with the board or shareholder resolution, subscription or loan agreement, source-of-funds evidence, ownership information, corporate documents, tax identification and any notarial or registry evidence required for the capital increase. Record equity contributions through the applicable Spanish corporate-law process and register capital changes where required. Do not route capital through personal accounts, unrelated third parties or the fund's client-money account. For non-euro currencies, document the FX rate, conversion spread, beneficiary amount and accounting entry. The sending and receiving banks may request information under AML, sanctions and balance-of-payments reporting rules; purpose-code selection must be consistent with the legal instrument and tax treatment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly documented through an MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or correspondent-bank payments. Require dual approval, beneficiary verification, invoice or contract support, sanctions screening and reconciliation before release. For trade in goods, retain purchase orders, commercial invoices, transport documents, customs documentation where applicable and proof of delivery. For services, retain the signed agreement, invoice, service evidence and withholding-tax analysis. A Commercial Letter of Credit may be arranged through an authorized bank for documentary trade, subject to UCP 600 or the agreed documentary-credit rules, bank limits, collateral and sanctions review. Investment-fund capital calls, subscriptions and distributions are not ordinary trade payments and should use separate payment templates, accounts and supporting documentation. SWIFT fees, correspondent deductions, value dates, cut-off times, rejected-payment procedures and beneficiary-name matching should be governed by a written treasury policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized bank for identified or highly probable operating, investment-management or fund-related exposures, supported by a documented hedging policy, exposure forecast, maturity and accounting treatment.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies subject to local convertibility or settlement restrictions, where legally permitted in the relevant jurisdiction and offered by an appropriately authorized counterparty. The SL must document the reference rate, fixing source, cash-settlement mechanics, collateral, counterparty exposure and suitability.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for recurring or longer-term currency funding exposures, subject to ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral terms, valuation, EMIR reporting and applicable clearing or margin requirements.

Foreign-exchange options or collars may be used for material, documented exposures where the bank approves the product and the SL understands premium, leverage, break-cost, collateral and accounting risks.

Hedging must not be used for unauthorized proprietary speculation or to disguise transfers between the GP, funds, investors and portfolio companies. Maintain board-approved limits, counterparty limits, confirmations, independent valuation, collateral controls, hedge documentation and periodic effectiveness testing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Deposit of Statutory Financial Statements (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales): balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, management report, audit report, and beneficial-ownership box (casilla 609)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the registered office; centralized data at the Registro Mercantil Central (Commercial Registry, Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the annual accounts within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); deposit with the Commercial Registry within 1 month after approval, i.e., no later than 31 July for calendar-year companies; anniversary rule applies to off-calendar fiscal years
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-deposit triggers cierre registral from the deposit deadline onward, blocking all subsequent corporate registrations (administrative strike-off equivalent); graduated administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 under Article 283.1 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital; two consecutive years of non-deposit allow coercive dissolution proceedings; defective UBO information is additionally sanctioned under AML Law 10/2010

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT, Spanish Central Tax Administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the 25th day of the 6th month following the end of the tax period; for calendar-year SLs the hard deadline is 25 July; off-calendar taxpayers follow the 6-month-plus-25-day anniversary rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior demand triggers the sliding recargo of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% of the amount due plus late-payment interest accruing from 26 July; additional flat and proportional penalties under Article 198 LGT up to 100% of omitted tax; intentional concealment above 25% of declared tax basis may trigger criminal referral under Article 305 of the Penal Code

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value-Added Tax Recapitulative Declaration (Declaración-Resumen Anual de IVA, Modelo 390)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 January following the calendar year in which VAT accrued; for non-calendar-year VAT periods, within 30 days after the close of the annual VAT period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers recargo of 5% to 20% of the VAT due plus late-payment interest; Article 198 LGT proportional penalties apply to omitted annual VAT data; access to VAT refund requests and monthly offsetting modalities is suspended until the annual recap is presented

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Summary of Withholding Tax Payments on Employment and Professional Income (Resumen Anual de Retenciones e Ingresos a Cuenta, Modelo 190)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the calendar year in which salaries, director fees, and professional service remunerations were paid and withheld; zero-filing is mandatory when the SL has withholding obligations even if no amounts were accrued
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Article 198 LGT penalties apply: EUR 200 flat fine for economically relevant information and proportional penalties of 2% to 20% on unreported withholding bases; repeated late filing can raise the flat fine to EUR 20,000; untimely presentation delays refund of excess withholdings and blocks issuance of creditor tax-residence certificates

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Related-Party Transaction Informative Return (Declaración de Operaciones Vinculadas, Modelo 232)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed during the month of November following the tax year (1–30 November); for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is due in November of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Article 198 LGT imposes a proportional penalty of 1% of the net amount of omitted related-party transactions when the data are not reported, subject to minima and maxima of EUR 300 and EUR 20,000 per year; failure to file also weakens transfer-pricing documentation and may trigger adjustment plus 20% penalty under Article 130 LGT

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate 25%; reduced rate 20% for SMEs with annual turnover ≤ €1 million; additional incentives for R&D investments, innovation, and qualifying startup equity under Spanish tax regimes

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 100 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via AEAT portal (Cl@ve or digital certificate)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25th day of the fourth month following fiscal year-end (e.g., 25 April for calendar-year companies)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before general deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Residents report worldwide income; non-residents report only Spanish-source income
N/A for residents; non-residents apply to Spanish permanent establishment income
Calculated at 25% on taxable base for Spanish-source income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: €100 per month late filing (minimum €100, maximum €1,500); criminal sanctions for evasion including fines up to five times evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% statutory rate; 0% for EU/EEA recipients under Council Directive 2011/96/EU
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain Treaty Relief Certificate (TRC) from AEAT; submit application form, DTA text, and beneficial ownership documentation to withholding agent prior to dividend payment
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 19% statutory for both royalties and interest; 0% under applicable DTAs including EU interest exemption under Council Directive 2003/49/EC for intra-EU transactions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Mandatory under Law 11/2018 and OECD ESR for high-risk activities including venture capital fund management; requires adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities in Spain

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate false declaration of income, expenses, or taxable base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties: fines up to five times evaded tax, imprisonment up to five years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability; disqualification from management, fines, and imprisonment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or submit local file/master file for related-party transactions exceeding €20 million revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Joint and several liability for penalties; potential criminal liability if intentional

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic Substance and Shell Company Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating Spanish SL without sufficient economic substance for venture capital activities or using as tax avoidance vehicle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of registration, fines up to €1 million, criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of corporate veil; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment for fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring transactions or failing to report suspicious activities in fund management and capital calls
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines €100,000 to €5 million or more; criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability including disqualification, fines, and possible imprisonment
